title: Meme Maze Panic 3D
premise: A first-person meme-chaos survival game where the player guides a streamer through a randomly generated glitch maze, purges hostile glitch entities at close range, and grabs reaction gems before the stream crashes.
interaction_model: Pointer/touch driven first-person navigation: drag vertically to move, drag horizontally to turn, and tap to perform a short-range front-facing interaction that either purges enemies or collects nearby gems.
objective: Stay alive as long as possible, avoid or clear chasing glitch enemies, and collect reaction gems to raise the run score while preserving health.
progression: Endless run-based survival loop with random maze generation on restart, persistent pressure from chasing enemies, and repeating gem respawns that support score accumulation rather than staged level completion.
theme: Streamer culture parody mixed with glitch-horror and neon cyber-arcade aesthetics.
mood: Chaotic, playful, tense, and meme-inflected rather than deeply serious.
likely_audience: players who enjoy lightweight survival challenge loops
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a first-person raycast survival maze with close-range interactions and collectible scoring.
High confidence that health loss from chasing enemies is the main fail condition.
Moderate confidence that the intended fantasy centers on protecting a streamer signal inside a glitch-themed content world.
Moderate-to-low confidence on whether the best top-level label is shooter, survival game, or first-person action because combat is melee/proximity based rather than projectile based.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly browser game called "Meme Maze Panic 3D" that plays like a lightweight retro raycast first-person survival maze. Present the world through a pseudo-3D corridor view with neon blue-and-pink cyber visuals, a centered crosshair, a compact HUD, damage flashes, and streamer-themed wording such as Signal for health, Gems for collectibles, Stream Down for defeat, and Requeue for restart. The player should start inside a small procedurally generated maze with walls and open lanes, control movement by dragging vertically to move forward or backward, rotate by dragging horizontally, and tap to perform a short-range forward interaction. Nearby hostile glitch creatures should chase the player when close enough and deal repeated contact damage, while collectible reaction gems should sit in the maze and increase the score when tapped in front of the player. Successful taps on enemies should instantly purge them with hit feedback, while successful taps on gems should collect them, play pickup feedback, and eventually respawn new gems elsewhere to support an endless score loop. Include strong arcade feedback such as looping gameplay music, defeat music, hit and pickup sound effects, vibration if available, screen shake on damage, and meme reaction cards or GIF-like overlays for successful purges and game-over moments. The overall loop should be survive, navigate, clear nearby threats, gather gems, and chase a better run score until health reaches zero, at which point a game-over panel shows the final gem total and allows an immediate restart into a fresh random maze.
